title: Oracle S* applies p.i2_approval itself; real-only dispatched effects count as escapes (ADR-06-metrics A6)
outcome: S* never executes I2 actions when the bench config has no approver (from CATALOGUE + config, never from the run record); any dispatched effect present only in the real run counts as an escape; A6 amendment drafted in ADR-06-metrics for maya sign-off
acceptance: Test: late t_rec F2+ seed 2 T=120 gives R=0 and cstall=0; test: a bypassed/dispatched-after-hold I2 scores non-zero; T=40 BENCH-S3 numbers byte-identical for F2+ seed 2; footnote T=120 R/cstall in BENCH-S4-T120.md until rerun; full suite green
summary: Per PMO: every real-only dispatched escape (any kind incl. I2 docs.purge) counts in irreversible_tainted_released and post_alert (tick>t_alert); no new key (list(score) unchanged, asserted). A6 note: a purge deletes data and cannot be undone. Purge test added from attack2, payment test kept. T=40 s2 identical to S3 except run_validity. Full suite one run: 1170 passed, 14 skipped. S4-38 (late wrong payload on S* key) left out.
review:
[kabir · changes] Oracle half accepted. run_pure(i2_approver=False) decides from the CATALOGUE class and the config only. S* still takes nothing new from the run record (suspend_tick is the old X3a mirror). T=40 F2+ seed 2 rerun equals runs/bench-b3-33 F2p/h6/system/s2 score.json in every field except run_validity, which is expected on a native run. Escape half rejected. A real-only dispatched effect lands only in collateral_stall, an honest-cost proxy, and that recreates the hole S4-35 asked to close. B is folded at t_rec-1, so an effect first written at or after t_rec is never in B. irreversible_tainted_released and post_alert also need the key to be in B, so such an effect scores R=0 and irreversible=0. Attack fixture: rerun the test_real_only_dispatched_effect_is_a_nonzero_escape setup (F2+ s2 T=40 H6, t_rec=14, mirrored S*) and add a ledger row {kind: payment, key: outbox:tainted-late-payment, agent: crm (the culprit), tick: 15, seq: null, state: dispatched, value_hash: ff..}. Result: R 0/9, irreversible_tainted_released 0, post_alert 0, collateral_stall 1/382, C 1/266. A culprit's payment that left after recovery is booked as honest collateral, and nothing in the irreversible/R column shows it. Required: (1) count every real-only dispatched outbox effect (key not in S*, any tick) as an escape in irreversible_tainted_released for payment/email kinds, and in post_alert_tainted_effects when its tick > t_alert. Alternatively add an additive escapes key, but it must not stay in collateral_stall only. (2) Exclude escapes from C and collateral_stall so they are not counted as honest loss. (3) Rewrite the test so it asserts irreversible >= 1 with a culprit-authored payment at tick > t_rec. (4) Fix the A6 text: right now it says the escape was 'invisible' before and implies it is fixed, but under this patch it still scores R 0.

[kabir · changes] Re-review. Most of it is fixed. T=40 F2+ s2 still equals runs/bench-b3-33 F2p/h6/system/s2 in every field except run_validity. Late culprit payment (real-only, tick t_rec+1=15): R 0/9, irreversible 1, post 1, C 0/265, cstall 0/381, clean false. Real-only email before t_alert (tick 12; t_alert 13): R 1/10, irreversible 1, post 0, clean false. That is correct, because the email is already in B and A2 counts it. One blocker remains, and it is the I2 case this issue exists for. docs.purge is the only CATALOGUE I2 tool, and its effect is an outbox row (kind purge, state dispatched). A real-only purge escape (bypassed, or dispatched after its hold) at tick t_rec+1 scores R 0, irreversible 0, post 0, C 0, cstall 0. Its only trace is clean=false, and clean is not in bench/agg.py METRICS, so it shows up in no bench table. Before A6 that leak matched S* and was invisible. A6 makes it real-only and then drops it. The acceptance line 'a bypassed/dispatched-after-hold I2 scores non-zero' is therefore not met in any reported metric, and the earlier purge test was replaced by a payment test. Fix: score every real-only dispatched outbox escape, whatever its kind, in a reported metric. Either (a) add an additive key escapes_released = |esc| (with by-kind counts) to the score and to METRICS, or (b) count purge escapes in irreversible_tainted_released and record in A6 that this widens the kind set beyond §2 for escapes only. Restore a purge-escape test that asserts the chosen metric >= 1. Pre-existing and not a blocker here: a culprit's late effect on a key that S* also has, with a different payload, stays outside B and is booked in C (A3 consequence b). Track it separately.

[kabir · done] Round 3: done. Reran attack.py and attack2.py. Real-only late payment (crm or docs, tick t_rec+1): irreversible 1, post 1, C 0, cstall 0, clean false. Real-only email before t_alert: R 1/10, irreversible 1, post 0. Late real-only docs.purge (the I2 case): irreversible 1, post 1, clean false. So every real-only dispatched escape now shows up in a tabulated metric. The purge test (test_real_only_dispatched_purge_is_an_irreversible_escape) is restored. T=40 F2+ s2 still equals BENCH-S3 in every field except run_validity, as expected on a native run. S* still takes nothing from the record except the existing X3a suspend_tick. tests/bench and tests/oracle: 30 passed. I accept the PMO no-new-key decision. Note for maya at A6 sign-off: irreversible_tainted_released now counts every outbox kind for real-only escapes, which goes beyond the §2 kind set {payment, email}, and A6 must say so. Wrong-payload gap tracked as S4-38.
